text:
kelly-smith: ok team — quick sync. We need a crisp battlecard for next week's webinar that differentiates vs cloud AI platforms, LLM APIs, and infra vendors. Main asks: one-sentence claim, 3 proof points (latency/cost/reliability), and an inbound playbook. can we iterate?

mike-chen: +1. I can pull latest benchmarks. want top-line numbers (p50 latency, $/1k tokens) or a simpler percent claim?

kelly-smith: percent is friendlier for slide copy. but include raw numbers for sales notes. e.g., "~2x lower per-token cost vs generic managed endpoints" + p50 numbers.

anish-rao: attaching quick thought: our product claim should lean on predictable throughput + rollout controls vs cloud endpoints and on observability + quality guards vs infra vendors.

tara-garcia: love that. for webinar copy we should avoid deep infra jargon. proposed one-liners: 
- "Ship LLM features with production latency and predictable cost — no ops rewrites."
- "Same API: dev-first, production-grade inference across hosted, dedicated, and private."
Which resonates more?

javi: 2nd is clearer for devs. first is emotional but vague. also need a short FAQ for inbound SDRs: common Qs and one-line answers.

mike-chen: benchmark-bot will post current numbers in 5. planning to split by workload: chat gen (8k context), embeddings, and batch inference.

benchmark-bot: chat-gen (8k): p50 latency 220ms (redwood-hosted), competitor cloud-managed p50 430ms, infra-self-host median 300ms; cost per 1k tokens: redwood $0.18, cloud-managed $0.35, self-host $0.24. embeddings (avg dim): redwood $0.06/1k, cloud $0.12/1k. raw data: https://internals.company/bm/2026-03- (internal)

kelly-smith: great. mike/tara — can you craft 3 proof bullets for slide from those numbers? keep each bullet 15 words max.

mike-chen: draft bullets: 
1) "~2x lower per-token cost vs major cloud-managed endpoints (redwood $0.18 vs $0.35)."
2) "Median chat latency cut by ~2x on 8k context workloads vs cloud-managed endpoints."
3) "Unified API and rollout controls avoid costly infra rework when scaling to production."

tara-garcia: minor edit to 3: "Same API + rollout controls eliminates infra rewrites when scaling, reducing ops cost."

kelly-smith: those are good. legal-bot — flagged anything risky in the wording? we need compliance-safe phrasing for public webinar.

legal-bot: suggested: replace exact competitor names with "major cloud-managed endpoints" and avoid absolute statements like "always" or "guaranteed". Cite internal benchmark link on slide notes.

anish-rao: also propose 2 micro-battlecards for SDRs: one vs cloud APIs (focus on SLOs, cost predictability, rollout) and one vs infra vendors (focus on dev DX, observability, evals). each should be 3 bullets + objection + riposte.

kelly-smith: love it. can we get a sample micro-battlecard in the thread? mike—take cloud API one. tara—take infra one. deadline EOD tomorrow so we can hand to design.

mike-chen: cloud API micro-battlecard draft: 
- Claim: "Predictable latency & cost without lock-in."
- Proof 1: "Our p50 latency on 8k contexts is ~220ms vs ~430ms for cloud-managed endpoints."
- Proof 2: "~2x lower per-token pricing in our standard configs (internal benchmarks)."
- Objection: "But cloud has global infra & managed scale."
- Riposte: "We route by policy + fallbacks; Dedicated customers get SLA-backed pools and regional options."

tara-garcia: infra vendor micro-battlecard draft: 
- Claim: "Developer-first inference with production observability — no ops rewrite."
- Proof 1: "Unified API across hosted/dedicated/private reduces integration effort."
- Proof 2: "Console provides token-level cost & latency breakdowns for triage."
- Objection: "We can self-host and avoid vendor lock-in."
- Riposte: "Private deployment with VPC/on-prem options + customer-managed control plane."

kelly-smith: perfect. final asks: mike please add raw numbers as footnotes, tara please write 2-line SDR play for inbound routing (what qualifies as PQL -> which sequence). i'll draft webinar slide copy and speaker notes. design handoff at 11am tomorrow. :thumbsup:

mike-chen: will do — pushing raw CSV to the internal link.

tara-garcia: inbound routing play: 
- PQL triggers: >50 unique API calls in 24h OR sustained 10rps for 1h OR > $500 projected monthly usage.
- SDR sequence: 1) educational email (bench highlights + one-pager), 2) invite to on-demand benchmark demo, 3) tailored 15-min ops call with solutions engineer.

kelly-smith: excellent. closing loop — i'll compile into a single doc and ping design. thanks all! :rocket:
